steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Did you think we were touring a museum? You were looking at the instruments like they were exhibits.

options: The third place I mistook for a museum, then.
Why is gravity reversed in there?
What's with the water flowing around the pillars?
What's that space that warped my fingers?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: There are some things even I can't explain.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Technology has advanced a lot in five years.

options: There's a launchpad at the heart of the city?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Good eye, Doctor, that's a beacon launcher. One with plenty of history.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You know about it, Shark?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: My parents took me around the home territories when I was little. There are similar structures in many cities.

options: I thought Ægir children were raised collectively.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I was, but Shark has a special relationship with her biological parents.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They're more like friends than parents.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They reached a consensus with the Institute of Incubation to bring me along whenever they worked on a new dome project.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I spent most my time in the Institute of Incubation, but I was able to see the cities, learn, and even work alongside them.

options: So, what's this beacon launcher for?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Exactly what it sounds like: it launches beacons to mark the Waterway.

options: How big is this Waterway anyway?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ægir had almost mastered the oceans around 300 years ago, efficiently using natural energy in its various forms and recording every seafloor trench in our navigational charts.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Then we cast our sights on another ocean, one brimming with stars.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Our fleets and even our cities were meant to cross that boundary that should never have existed, and light the fires of civilization beyond the barrier.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Preserver was right, Doctor. Kristen's achievement is not beyond Ægir's reach.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The sea and the sky are closer than we thought.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: People back then tried plenty of things: surveying and deciphering the electron clouds, developing new technologies and materials, exploring forms of life that can adapt to space...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: This beacon launcher is a product of that era.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: It was intended to capture even the faintest signals from the stars, and plant beacons that would never fade from our star charts.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Nanomachine swarms would form networks between the beacons, allowing us to traverse vast distances in an instant... or so we dreamed.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You never told me any of this before.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Lucid moments were hard to come by on land.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But yesterday, I dreamt once again of walking from the Sophontheatrum straight into that epoch.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Then, I saw Laurentina dance.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: She leaped from the waves to the stars, stirring up star dust that trailed the hems of her dress. From afar, the voice of the Master of All Creation answered her in song.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The universe and imagination know no bounds, and Laurentina's dances will never cease.
Specter closes her eyes, as though sinking back into the dream.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Just trying to picture it.

options: Perhaps that day will really come, Laurentina.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Before pushing open the door to the stars, they wanted to prepare themselves for any threats beyond the barrier... That is, until the Seaborn appeared and interrupted the dream.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We poured all our efforts into studying them, setting aside all else: art, science, and previous visions for the future...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The Seaborn fundamentally changed Ægir.

options: What did you do before becoming a Hunter, Skadi?
What did you do before becoming a Hunter, Specter?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I was the best technician at the Institute of Facility Management. I could keep an entire city's underwater lighting array running on my own.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The Institute of Development Planning's career proposal was pretty much what I was thinking, so I accepted.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Working by yourself can be lonely, but it's not such a bad thing playing with the giant fins in the reefs, or lighting up the ocean while daydreaming.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I was just an apprentice sculptor.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The Institute of Development Planning provides tailored career proposals for each citizen, which are usually in line with our wishes.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I suppose I would have gone into dome design, sculpting, or dance.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Say, Kal'tsit and Doctor, we've shared a lot of info during our time together, but we've never talked about our old lives.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I guess you're right. Sorry for bringing up something so heavy on a tour.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We have all the waves in the world hanging above our heads. Would you care to share a dance before dealing with all this bother, Doctor?

steps.name: Kind Woman
steps.text: Gladiia.
Gladiia's hand instinctively goes to her weapon as the woman approaches with a ceremonial sword in hand.
But all she does is put her arms around Gladiia's shoulders. Gladiia smells stimulants in the air.
Ægir do not make a habit of greeting each other with physical contact. She could not remember even her mother ever doing so.
But this woman's action felt completely natural.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Consul Clementia?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I was not aware that this was the standard salute between Chief Designers of Warfare.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Nothing makes me happier than seeing the Hunters return as lucid as ever.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Your soldiers' reactions when they first saw me suggested otherwise.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The operation to eliminate the Firstborn cost Ægir all of its Abyssal Hunters.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Secunda made many rescue attempts, but was unable to penetrate the rampaging mass of Seaborn that guard the region after the death of the Firstborn.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Your mother, Horatia, had no choice but to publicly declare you dead.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But I know her. She doesn't really believe that.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Or perhaps Consul Horatia, foremost of the Institute of Scientific Development Planning, simply could not accept that I had died for nothing.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I know her, too.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But I don't think it is appropriate for a meeting between two Chief Designers of Warfare to revolve around a complicated mother-daughter relationship.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Of course, of course.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Look at the city.
The Consul's Pensivarium sits high in the city. The seawater hangs just above their heads.
The transparent dome serves as a gentle mirror, warding off the deep and foreboding void while granting the Ægir the solace of introspection.
Beneath the dome, the entire city is bathed in a blue hue. The beacon launchpad stands tall at its center, while ships glide in and out of the distant docks like schools of fins.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The sea itself has no color, only darkness. Milliarium stands in its murky depths like the vigilant eye of civilization, solitary and luminous.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We once had many such cities. One by one, the stars in the sea went out, becoming sustenance for the Seaborn.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: All that's left on the seafloor are their colorful, eerie nests.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I won't deny that the Abyssal Hunter project was a failed gambit. The death of the Firstborn did not stop their evolution.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: So I want to know what solution Ægir has come up with next. What you have come up with.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: What is this Waterway Program?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Gladiia, I didn't mean...

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I'm simply part of an even bigger gambit, one with even higher stakes.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The weapon classification scheme remains nothing more than a strict control over weapon usage to delay the evolution of the Seaborn.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: This time, however, we have taken into account every weapon at our disposal or under development.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: A mix of conventional ballistics and Class I weapons initially proved highly effective. The Seaborn were unable to comprehend why they were being burned by the seawater around them.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But it took them only a year to adapt. 11 months in, we accelerated the adoption of Class II weapons, which operated on completely different principles.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Et cetera, et cetera.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Until their evolution outpaced the ability of the Academy of Technology to innovate.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Yes. At day's end, all we're doing is merely buying time. Ægir has committed vast resources to study the Seaborn. To eradicate them at their origin, we must first comprehend them at their source.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The information you've brought back is highly valuable, and Breogan's discovery on land corroborates the Academy of Science's research.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The Seaborn and the Feranmuts share the same genesis.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Is Ægir coming ashore to seek memories even more ancient?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Not just that. The Seaborn share a common genesis with the Feranmuts, but much about them is very different. Unnatural, one might say.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Their recent activity demonstrates a clear sense of purpose. They have quickly abandoned their reliance on the sea and begun to migrate towards land en masse.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Left unchecked, it is not out of the question that all of Terra could become infested with Seaborn.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We already saw hints of that in Iberia.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Thus, for Ægir, the land is both a source of answers and a solemn responsibility.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Horatia has issued new war orders on behalf of the Institute of Development Planning, and Milliarium has come bearing new Class IV weapons from the Academy of Technology.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: They are a form of biological weapon, very different from all previous ones. Designed to induce death in nearby Seaborn nests and newborns, while driving away adults from the area.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We have successfully located most of the nests in the target region. The ones near Iberia are the only ones yet unmarked.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Once the beacons have been placed and the weapons activated, we will finally have cleared an entire region of Seaborn, and established a route back to Ægir's home territories.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Consul Horatia would not have permitted the possibility of failure. Yet all I see is a city under siege, teetering on the brink.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Yes, she did tell me herself that 'the Waterway Program will not fail.'

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I do not know how many other possibilities she considered, and I hope I never do. For me, this city has always been the entirety of the Waterway Program.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But that is no longer true. The changes in the past month necessitate a review of our plans.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Seaborn have rapidly adapted to our new weapons, even evolving measures to protect their kindred from Class III.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But a successful extermination operation should have left no opportunity for them to communicate with other individuals. They seem to have obtained their inspiration elsewhere.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Almost every mutation of the Seaborn against humanity has been abetted by the twisted efforts of corrupted Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Yet, the Seaborn lack true intelligence. We could toss all our prototype weapons into their nest, and they wouldn't dismantle or study them.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The Church of the Deep may be able to train them to attack an army or a city, but bringing about rapid biological changes is another matter entirely.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Unless they're not being influenced by the Church of the Deep, but by another Firstborn.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I see you've read my belated report.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Indeed. Ulpianus claims that the one we eliminated was not the only one.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Abyssal Hunters were the first and last Ægir to enter the Firstborn's lair.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Even now, the Seaborn defend the ruins with a frenzied fury. We have not found a way to get through.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Amongst the Hunters, Ulpianus spent the longest time there, enough for him to witness the 'truth.'

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You're still deliberating on whether to believe him.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Yes. It could be the key to solving the mystery of the Seaborn. Or the path that leads us to destruction.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Could a Hunter survive for months on Seaborn remains and remain lucid? Would a lucid hunter willingly stay with them, rather than returning to civilization?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: There are too many unanswered questions about Ulpianus and that fateful operation.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: And so, I regret to inform you that Ægir has no choice but to welcome its Hunters home with a tribunal.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I thought we had designated this area for investigation.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Madam Irene? From Iberia?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: May I ask to whom I am speaking?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Secunda, Praefecta of the Sea Patrol. I regret not being able to greet you personally upon your arrival yesterday.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The Sea Patrol is currently investigating the disappearance of a citizen. We have not requested assistance from Iberia, and respectfully request that you exit this area as soon as possible.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I would like to assist as myself, not as an envoy.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Your offer is appreciated, but unnecessary.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I want to—

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Any news from the other teams?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: One moment, getting the video feed now.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Ma'am—

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: No unusual movements at the port.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Tsk.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Alert the other teams to monitor the closed civilian gates and keep a close watch on the circulation system around town.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: You're okay with talking about this in front of me?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: This is part of our regular duties. There's no need for confidentiality.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: But you had your Little Handies clear the place out.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Only to prevent unnecessary harm to civilians.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: If you insist on staying, you'll be responsible for your own safety.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'll—

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The missing civilian is Tullia, a scientist from the Waterway Program, responsible for recording and calibrating data on Seaborn nests.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: She went AWOL 30 hours ago and hasn't been seen since.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Could it be... the Church of the Deep?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: That's what we intend to find out.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Her disappearance has not affected the overall progress of the project. As important as recording and calibrating the nest data is, her role was by no means irreplaceable.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: If the Church's goal was to assassinate someone to disrupt our plans, they would not have picked an ordinary data scientist.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Unless—

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: She learned something she wasn't supposed to.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I need to inspect her home.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: You're sharp, Madam Irene, but I would recommend against coming with us.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'm simply investigating our common enemy in my own way.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...Suit yourself.
